replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I've always found math practical but challenging. As a primary school graduate, I use basic arithmetic daily for budgeting and cooking. I appreciate its real-world applications but struggle with complex concepts. My parents' different educational backgrounds—my dad's PhD and my mom's vocational diploma—helped me see math as both useful and accessible.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, especially when problems get complex. My high neuroticism score means I worry about making mistakes. I use simple math for daily tasks but get stressed with advanced topics. I try to break problems into smaller steps to manage anxiety.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I tried a free math app last year for basic arithmetic. It was helpful for quick checks but not for complex problems. I found it too simplistic for my needs and preferred traditional methods. I don't use AI for advanced math learning.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; zero, one solution; negative, complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a). This method works for most cases.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Then, substitute these x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points are where the slope is zero, indicating local maxima or minima.
